title: Upper bounded derived module objects admit projective models
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $C\in D(A)$ be an object of the derived category of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $b\in\mathbf Z$. If $H^i(C)=0$ for all $i>b$, there is a cochain complex $L^\bullet$ of projective $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] with $L^i=0$ for $i>b$ and an isomorphism $Q(L^\bullet)\cong C$ in $D(A)$, where $Q$ is the localization of complexes.

source.place: Tag 0646, lemma-projective-resolutions-exist, parts (2) and (3), for the category of modules; Tag 0645, lemma-cohomology-bounded-above

proof.text: The cohomology bound says C is in the standard D^{≤b}. Mathlib DerivedCategory.isLE_iff and exists_iso_Q_obj_of_isLE give a complex K strictly zero above b and an isomorphism C ≅ Q(K). This is good upper truncation of any representative.

Every module M is a quotient of the free module on its underlying set: the map sends e_m to m and is onto since m is the image of e_m. Free modules are projective, so ModuleCat A has enough projectives (Mathlib ModuleCat.enoughProjectives). Taking opposites turns projective presentations into injective presentations. Thus (ModuleCat A)ᵒᵖ has enough injectives; this uses only duality of the lifting definitions.

source.place: ModuleCat.enoughProjectives; Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Preadditive/Injective/Basic.lean, enough injectives in the opposite of a category with enough projectives

proof.text: Apply CochainComplex.opEquivalence to op K, combining categorical opposite with the index reversal n ↦ -n. The result K' is strictly zero below -b. Use the exact-bound unbundled Mathlib theorem CochainComplex.Plus.modelCategoryQuillen.exists_quasiIso_injective underlying [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution-existence]: there are a complex J, an injective object J^n in every degree, and a quasi-isomorphism f:K' → J, with J strictly zero below -b.

source.place: exists_quasiIso_injective, lines 668 onward; dual route in Stacks derived.tex Tag 0646, lemma-projective-resolutions-exist

proof.text: Apply the inverse opposite equivalence to f and unop. It gives g:L → K'', where L^n = (J^{-n})ᵘⁿᵒᵖ. To check QuasiIso g, fix n and use the short complexes in degrees (n-1,n,n+1). The corresponding short-complex map is exactly unopMap of f in degrees (-(n+1),-n,-(n-1)). This is a quasi-isomorphism since f is one, and ShortComplex.quasiIso_unopMap preserves it. This is the private helper quasiIso_unop_reverse.

Injectivity of J^{-n} in the opposite category gives categorical projectivity of L^n. Mathlib ModuleCat.projective_of_module_projective converts it to Module.Projective A (L.X n); the required Small instance holds in max u v. If b<n then -n<-b, so J^{-n}, hence L^n, is zero. The unopped unit of CochainComplex.opEquivalence identifies K'' with K. Q inverts g, giving Q(L) ≅ Q(K'') ≅ Q(K) ≅ C. Every bound and universe is unchanged.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0645 and 0646: use the stated duality with bounded-below injective resolutions, implemented by Mathlib exact-bound exists_quasiIso_injective and CochainComplex.opEquivalence; quasi-isomorphism transfer checked on short complexes.
